checked_sources: Independent exact replay: build edge masks and endpoint prerequisites, scan 20-bit masks, remove upset(max(I)) using endpoint adjacency, and form the least common multiple of the distinct cycle lengths.
correctness.rationale: An ideal is uniquely a vertex subset U and any subset of its induced edges, giving H=F(t,1+t). Equal cubic triangle-free counts agree through triples, and m(U)=12-3|V\U|+m(V\U) handles sizes at least five. For four-sets, the independent-set counts are 2 and 0, and the induced squares number 6 and 4. In the Wagner graph a square must use two disjoint opposite chords and parallel cycle edges (0 or 1 chord cannot close in four steps, three or four cannot lie in a four-cycle because the chords are a matching); the cube squares are its faces. Counting all four-sets and occurrences of single edges and pairs of edges gives the three common equations for the intervening coefficients, hence difference (2,-8,12,-8,2). Independently ran an exhaustive Python enumeration, different from the supplied checker: scan all 2^20 subsets for each graph, dropping any that include an edge but omit an endpoint; map each valid I to P minus the upset of max(I), which is inverse rowmotion because maximal elements of the generated ideal are exactly its complement-minimal generators. Verify the inverse images give exactly the ideal set; traverse the cycles and count ranks directly. This reproduced both complete histograms in RESULT.md, all ideal/orbit/max-length counts and both automorphism orders (also independently enumerated over 8! permutations). The computed LCMs are 110880 and 244379520, ratio 2204, and the directly enumerated rank defect is (8,+2).
residual_risks: The supplied script prints the full histograms and asserts aggregate features; it does not hard-code equality with every printed bucket. The independent traversal explicitly matched both full printed lists. Neither finite enumeration is a theorem for a larger graph class.

checked_sources: RESULT.md full rank and orbit comparisons
value.rationale: The cube and Wagner graph are standard, comparably small connected vertex-transitive cubic graphs; the shared parameters force almost all of their incidence-ideal rank data to match. The contrast between a single two-ideal discrepancy and a 2204-fold order change is a concrete test of how little those near-equal static statistics constrain the order of the dynamics. The exact census is a usable benchmark for methods computing classical rowmotion on graph incidence posets, where full rather than sampled profiles matter.
residual_risks: This is a paired witness with equal ranks except for one degree, not an example with exactly identical rank polynomials or a theorem on all cubic graphs.
